report_name: Wiz Report: Cloud Incidents Surge 60% in H1 2026

threat_actors.name: TeamPCP
threat_actors.description: A financially motivated group observed conducting supply-chain attacks against npm and PyPI ecosystems by poisoning developer packages to achieve credential theft.

threat_actors.name: North Korean actors
threat_actors.description: State-sponsored actors from North Korea engaged in software supply-chain attacks, including trojanizing the 'axios' package, with likely motives of espionage and financial gain.

threat_actors.name: JINX-0163
threat_actors.description: A newly emerged cloud-native extortion gang that specializes in targeting and compromising non-human identities, such as cloud service accounts and IAM roles, to gain broad environmental access and demand a ransom.

attack_patterns.name: Compromise Software Supply Chain
attack_patterns.description: Used by threat actors like TeamPCP and North Korean actors to poison open-source packages in ecosystems like npm and PyPI. Malicious packages with names similar to legitimate ones were used to trick developers into installing them, leading to credential theft.

attack_patterns.name: Cloud Accounts
attack_patterns.description: Used by the JINX-0163 extortion group to compromise non-human cloud identities, such as service accounts and IAM roles, to gain an initial foothold in victim cloud environments.

attack_patterns.name: Resource Hijacking
attack_patterns.description: Attackers deployed cryptominers, such as xmrig and kinsing, after exploiting vulnerabilities in AI infrastructure to use the victim's compute resources.

malware.name: Xmrig
malware.description: A common cryptomining process observed running on compromised servers, particularly those hosting AI models like Langflow.

malware.name: Kinsing
malware.description: A common cryptomining process observed running on compromised servers, particularly those hosting AI models.

indicators.name: Cryptominer Process Execution (Xmrig, Kinsing)
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: Cryptominer Process Execution (Xmrig, Kinsing)
id: 5e8b1c2a-9d3f-4e6a-8c1b-2d3e4f5a6b7c
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of common cryptomining processes xmrig or kinsing, often deployed after exploiting cloud infrastructure.
references:
  - https://www.wiz.io/blog/cloud-threat-highlights-h1-2026
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-07
tags:
  - attack.t1496
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/xmrig'
      - '/kinsing'
    OriginalFileName:
      - 'xmrig'
      - 'kinsing'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Unlikely, but could be legitimate if cryptomining is authorized.
indicators.description: Detects the execution of common cryptomining processes xmrig or kinsing, which the report notes are deployed on compromised AI infrastructure.

indicators.name: Developer Credential File Access
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: Developer Credential File Access
id: a1b2c3d4-e5f6-4a90-8bcd-ef1234567890
status: experimental
description: Detects access to developer credential files (.npmrc, .pypirc) which may indicate credential theft attempts by malicious packages.
references:
  - https://www.wiz.io/blog/cloud-threat-highlights-h1-2026
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-07
tags:
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1552.001
level: medium
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '/.npmrc'
      - '/.pypirc'
  filter_legit:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/npm'
      - '/pip'
      - '/python'
  condition: selection and not filter_legit
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate developer tools or scripts reading configuration.
indicators.description: Detects access to developer credential files like .npmrc and .pypirc, which is a sign of credential theft as conducted by groups like TeamPCP.
